item.title: Kerry county councillor accuses An Post of failing to meet obligations in West Kerry
item.description: A Kerry county councillor has accused An Post of failing to meet its service obligations to deliver post in West Kerry. Sinn Fein councillor for the Castleisland-Corca Dhuibhne Municipal District, Robert Brosnan, wants the Minister for Communications to intervene. He argues that the delays in postal deliveries to the Inch and Annascaul areas are being caused by restructuring within An Post, in which the sorting office was relocated to Monavalley in Tralee. item.title: Average secondary school student in Kerry missed almost 19 days per year
item.description: The average secondary school student in Kerry missed almost 19 (18.89) days per school year. That’s according to new research from the Economic and Social Research Institute, which shows that high levels of school absence remain a national concern, with little improvement since the pandemic. The ESRI study, covering the 2022–23 and 2023–24 school years, found that around one in five students nationally miss 20 days or more of school each year. item.title: Improvements to Ring of Kerry bridge to take place this tourist season
item.description: A Kerry County Councillor has claimed ‘fish seem to be more important than people’ after learning that works will take place on a Ring of Kerry bridge during the tourist season. Independent councillor Johnny Healy-Rae raised the issue at the recent meeting of Kenmare Municipal District. Improvements to the Cummergorm Bridge, located on the N70, are required to go ahead during peak tourism season, outside of the fish migration months. item.title: 37 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry
item.description: There are 37 patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry today. That’s according to figures from the Irish Nurses’ and Midwives’ Organisation. They show there are 19 patients waiting on a trolley in UHK’s emergency department, while a further 18 people are waiting on trolleys in wards within the hospital. item.title: Swans and cattle among animals which caused ESB outages in Kerry
item.description: Swans, cattle, crows, and a seagull are among the animals which caused ESB outages for thousands of customers in Kerry last year. Data released to journalist Ken Foxe from ESB Networks under the Freedom of Information Act, seen by Radio Kerry, outlines the outages caused by animals last year. On St Patrick’s Day last year, a swan caused an outage in Ballyard in Tralee, which affected 111 customers in the area. item.description: Radio Kerry has joined a new digital audio platform Vocalise which has been launched by IRS+ and digital media sales house Digitize. item.title: Proposed developments to Killorglin town approved after significant criticism
item.description: Proposed developments to Killorglin town have been approved after facing significant criticism. Kerry County Council received over 100 submissions from residents and local businesses, which were raised at the recent Kenmare Municipal District meeting. Some of the main concerns include loss of parking and traffic congestion. item.title: Over 23% increase in number of patients on trolleys in UHK in January
item.description: The number of patients waiting on trolleys in University Hospital Kerry has jumped by almost a quarter in a year. That’s according to figures from the Irish Nurses’ and Midwives’ Organisation for January. The figures show over 13,000 (13,077) people were waiting on trolleys in hospitals across the country during the first month of 2026.
